subject: Realtime API: elevated 5xx/429 + timeouts — exec brief & mitigation plan

Subject: Realtime API — spike of 5xx/429 & client timeouts (affecting checkout)

Hi Rachel,

We kicked off a hotfix window after seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses from the Realtime API starting ~07:50 PDT. Our checkout flows are timing out for ~30% of requests and we had to route traffic to a degraded mode.

What we observed:
- 5xx rate rose from ~0.2% to 6% between 07:50–08:05
- 429 rate climbed to ~4% and persisted until ~08:20
- End-to-end timeouts reported by clients (30s) — many retries from our SDKs seemed to amplify the issue

We attached sample traces and dashboard screenshots. This is impacting many customers in our US region. Please advise immediate mitigations and ETA to stabilize.

Thanks,
Alex Turner

Nimble Retail

Subject: RE: Realtime API — spike of 5xx/429 & client timeouts (affecting checkout)

Quick incident summary from ops:
- Timeline: At ~07:46 we saw a sudden increase in tail latency on the Realtime frontend fleet servicing long-sequence requests (mostly >512 tokens).
- Root cause (current hypothesis): A regressed cache invalidation path in the prefix/KV cache service caused a burst of cache misses, which increased downstream model server load. Simultaneously many client SDKs performed aggressive retries (exp backoff misconfigured), leading to a retry amplification loop and elevated 429s from the autoscaler protection layer.

Actions taken (already):
1) Disabled aggressive client-side retry guidance in the SDK via remote config (rolled at 08:00).
2) Temporarily raised per-customer concurrency cap for Nimble Retail and enabled fallback to quantized model variant to reduce per-token CPU.
3) Autoscaler rules adjusted to allow a modest burst (10% headroom) to reduce 429s while we validate.
4) Kicked off a targeted cache warm-up for hot prefixes.

Immediate next steps (15–60m):
- Rollback risky cache invalidation patch (if present) and add a canary fix. Owner: Stephanie.
- Add burn-rate alert for error budget (INF-789). Owner: Sean.
- Provide Nimble a short status note with mitigations and ETA for full recovery (Rachel).

Attachment: incident traces and preliminary flamegraphs included.

--
Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 12:30:22 -0700
Subject: RE: Realtime API — spike of 5xx/429 & client timeouts (affecting checkout)

Detailed remediation and follow-ups (internal):

What happened
- A recent optimization to reduce cache write latency introduced a path that aggressively evicted certain hot keys under contention. Under a bursty customer workload this produced higher-than-expected cache miss ratios and increased load on the model serving tier.
- Autoscaler protection correctly rate-limited when CPU queue latencies crossed threshold, producing 429s for excess requests rather than higher 5xx rates.

Gaps identified
- Alerting: We do not have a burn-rate alert that correlates error budget depletion to increased retry rates — added to INF-789 backlog.
- Runbooks: The Realtime runbook lacks a specific playbook for cache-invalidation regressions and for guiding temporary client retry guidance changes.
- SLOs: Per-customer concurrency SLAs are conservative; we should model tail latency under burst scenarios and consider an adaptive SLO for long-sequence workloads.

Planned remediation (owners & ETA)
- Revert/patch cache-invalidation logic and deploy a canary: Owner Stephanie / ETA 3h.
- Create a short runbook section for prefix/KV cache incidents and client retry guidance: Owner Marissa / ETA 2d.
- Add burn-rate and retry-amplification alerts plus a dashboard widget: Owner Sean / ETA 24h.
- Model variant fallback: formalize policy to fallback to quantized variant automatically under sustained high token-per-request patterns: Owner Engineering (Stephanie) / ETA 5d.
- Capacity planning: schedule a dedicated capacity run to analyze burst headroom and autoscaler tuning: Owner Markus / ETA 1w.

Temporary remediation already in place should stabilize requests; monitoring shows 5xx back to ~0.5% by 11:45 and 429s steadily dropping. We'll validate over the next 24h.

Stephanie
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Subject: Post-incident: Realtime API timeout wave — summary & next steps

Alex — thanks again for the quick heads-up on Sunday. Below is a short summary for your execs and next steps. Happy to jump on a call tomorrow if useful.

Executive summary
- Impact: Nimble Retail experienced increased timeouts and elevated 5xx/429 rates from 07:46–~11:30 PDT on 2026-07-12, primarily affecting long-sequence Realtime requests used by checkout (estimated 20–30% increase in failed requests during the window).
- Cause: Cache invalidation regression created higher cache miss ratios, amplifying load on model servers; client retry amplification contributed to sustained pressure and elevated 429s from autoscaler protections.
- Mitigation: We rolled back the cache invalidation change in a canary, warmed hot prefixes, adjusted autoscaler headroom, and pushed an SDK remote config to reduce aggressive retries. Service metrics returned to baseline by ~11:45 PDT.

Planned follow-ups (owners / ETA):
- Full postmortem doc and timeline (Stephanie / 48h) — will include impact quantification and code-level root cause.
- New runbook section for cache-invalidation incidents & retry guidance (Marissa / 2d).
- Burn-rate + retry-amplification alerts (Sean / 24h).
- Policy to auto-fallback to quantized model variant under sustained high-token workloads (Engineering / 5d).
- Capacity analysis for autoscaler tuning & burst headroom (Markus / 1w).

Goodwill credit: Markus is preparing a suggested credit; we'll follow up with your billing contact.

Next steps: I'll send the formal postmortem link when ready and propose a 60-minute review early next week.

Thanks for patience and for the partnership — we know checkout reliability is critical.

Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
